note: Cases mirror the Rust tests of the @user.<field> existence checks. user_identity.rs: a_viewer_field_reads_in_every_identity_environment (the first five cases), an_identity_row_field_reads_only_where_the_roster_declares_it (the next four). tests/user_identity_validation.rs: without_a_declared_identity_entity_an_unknown_field_is_still_an_error and its default-shape control, reading_an_undeclared_identity_field_is_an_error, and the sourceEntityDefinition provenance test. tests/entity_access_validation.rs: an_unknown_user_field_reuses_the_identity_error_code (the policy cases). tests/expectations_validation.rs: a_user_field_outside_the_declared_shape_fails_standalone, slice_with_expects_identity_validates_clean, a_trait_guard_outside_the_declared_shape_fails_standalone, without_expects_an_unknown_user_field_keeps_todays_verdict, an_imported_bodys_user_reads_are_not_checked_against_the_declaration, an_authored_traits_user_reads_are_checked_against_the_declaration, and under_declared_identity_expectation_fails_even_when_a_real_roster_exists with its covering, over-declaring and shapeless controls. Differences from the compiler: findings inside one trait follow the key order of the lowered program, where the compiler follows the order of its trait struct (the same set); the Viewer members come from the installed language facts fed here as FACTS_HEARD.

findings.message: `@user.teamId` is not a field of the [identity] entity `Person`. It resolves to null, so every branch reading it silently takes its negative arm.
findings.suggestion: Declare `teamId` on entity Person, or read one of: claims, email, id, name, permissions, role, tier

findings.message: `@user.teamId` is not part of the default identity shape (claims, email, id, name, permissions, role). No [identity] entity is declared, so nothing can carry this field — it resolves to null and every branch reading it silently takes its negative arm.
findings.suggestion: Declare an [identity] entity carrying `teamId`, or read one of: claims, email, id, name, permissions, role
